bug_description.original: A heap overflow exists in coap_pdu_parse_opt() in pdu.c due to coap_opt_length() not being called with next_option_safe(), which allows out-of-bound reads for malformed options.
bug_description.normalized: The libFuzzer target passes an attacker-controlled UDP CoAP packet into `coap_pdu_parse()`. The parser copies the exact 259-byte witness into a heap-backed `coap_pdu_t`, derives a 255-byte options region after the 4-byte UDP header, and enters `coap_pdu_parse_opt()` with `token_length == 0`. The witness options region is 254 single-byte `0x20` option headers followed by one trailing `0x6e`. After the loop safely consumes the 254 `0x20` bytes, only that final `0x6e` header remains. The vulnerable code calls `coap_opt_length(opt)` before `next_option_safe()` / `coap_opt_parse()` has checked whether the remaining extent can encode a full option. `coap_opt_length()` interprets the low nibble `0x0e` as an extended option length, consumes one extra byte from the buffer's spare capacity, then reads the second required extension byte one byte past the 262-byte heap allocation. AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow read at `src/option.c:266`. The fix reverses the order: it first calls `next_option_safe()` and only computes `len` from the already-validated option when `optsize != 0`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled CoAP packet bytes into the heap-backed PDU buffer later parsed as options.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 259-byte packet `50 20 20 20` + `20` repeated 254 times + final byte `6e`. After the 4-byte UDP header, the copied 255-byte body is therefore 254 one-byte `0x20` option headers followed by a lone trailing `0x6e` option header.

sink.description: ASan crash site. Fallthrough from extended-length decoding performs the second option-length extension-byte read after `opt` has already advanced to the first byte past the heap allocation.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 1` in `coap_opt_length /src/libcoap/src/option.c:266:15`, at address `0x6120000008c6`, which is 0 bytes to the right of the 262-byte region `[0x6120000007c0, 0x6120000008c6)`.

root_cause.description: The option parser computes the option length from the raw option pointer before validating that the remaining `length` bytes are sufficient for a complete option encoding.
root_cause.note: On the witnessed final iteration only one byte remains, but line 702 still calls `coap_opt_length(opt)` before line 703's `next_option_safe(&opt, &length, &pdu->max_opt)`. If line 703 ran first, `coap_opt_parse(opt, 1, ...)` would hit `ADVANCE_OPT_CHECK` in the case-14 length branch and return 0 without reading any extension byte. The fix makes that safe parse happen first and derives `len` only from a validated option.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant bytes are the copied option stream stored in the PDU buffer. The final copied byte `0x6e` is later reinterpreted as an extended-length option header.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Exact witness bytes: 4-byte UDP header `50 20 20 20`, then 254 body bytes `0x20`, then final body byte `0x6e`.

parser_admitted.condition: The exact witness header bytes `50 20 20 20` make `coap_pdu_parse_header()` set `token_length = 0` and `code = 0x20`, while `coap_pdu_parse()` sets `used_size = 255` after the fixed 4-byte UDP header. The token-length rejection therefore does not fire and the non-empty-message branch enters the options loop.

crashing_option_reached.condition: In the exact witness, each of the first 254 option bytes is `0x20`, so every successful `next_option_safe` iteration consumes exactly one byte and advances `opt` by one. When `pdu->max_opt` reaches 4 and 16 the later semantic checks log `option ... has bad length 0` and only set `good = 0`, so the loop still reaches the final one-byte `0x6e` option with `length == 1`.

coarse_trace.summary: libcoap copies the attacker-controlled UDP packet into a heap-backed PDU, derives a 255-byte post-header body, parses `token_length == 0` from the header, and enters option parsing at the start of that body.

The option loop safely advances across 254 leading `0x20` one-byte options, leaving a final single-byte `0x6e` header with `length == 1`, then calls `coap_opt_length(opt)` before the bounds-safe `next_option_safe()` check.

The final `0x6e` header is decoded as an extended option length: the first extension-byte read lands on the buffer's one spare payload byte and the second extension-byte read crosses the 262-byte heap allocation, triggering ASan.

fine_trace.note: Before parsing begins, the PDU allocator clamps payload capacity to 256 bytes and uses a 6-byte header margin. For the exact 259-byte witness this yields a 262-byte heap region with `pdu->token` 6 bytes into it, so there is exactly one payload-capacity byte beyond the later 255-byte message body.

Source. This copies the exact 259-byte witness into the PDU buffer from step 1. Bytes 0-3 are the UDP header `50 20 20 20`; the 255 copied body bytes are 254 `0x20` option headers followed by a final `0x6e`. Because only 255 body bytes are copied into 256 bytes of payload capacity, `pdu->token[255]` remains untouched and only the message bytes up to `pdu->token[254]` are initialized from input.

For the fixed `COAP_PROTO_UDP` call path, `coap_pdu_parse_header_size()` returns 4. The parser therefore records `pdu->used_size = 259 - 4 = 255`, which is the remaining byte extent that should bound option parsing after the UDP header.

The copied header byte `0x50` yields `pdu->token_length = 0`, and header byte `0x20` yields nonzero message code `0x20` (`1.00`). The vulnerable path therefore stays in the non-empty-message branch and does not skip directly to `pdu->used_size = 0`.

fine_trace.code:
coap_opt_t *opt = pdu->token + pdu->token_length;
    size_t length = pdu->used_size - pdu->token_length;
fine_trace.note: With `token_length == 0` and `used_size == 255`, option parsing starts at `opt = pdu->token` and treats the full 255-byte post-header body as remaining option data.

Across the first 254 loop iterations, each leading `0x20` byte is parsed as a one-byte option with delta 2 and length 0, so `next_option_safe()` advances `opt` by one byte and decrements `length` by one each time. The debug logs for options 4 and 16 come from the later `bad:` label at lines 740-743, which only sets `good = 0`; it does not return. By the final iteration, `opt` points to the last body byte `0x6e` and `length == 1`.

Root cause. On the final iteration from step 6, only the single header byte `0x6e` remains, but line 702 still calls `coap_opt_length(opt)` before the safe parser at line 703 has validated the option extent. The function receives only the raw pointer, not the remaining `length == 1` bound.

The call from step 7 reaches the extended-length branch because the low nibble of the final header byte `0x6e` is `0x0e`. After line 255's unconditional `++opt` skips past that header, line 263 reads the first length-extension byte from `pdu->token[255]`, the one spare allocated payload byte described in step 1, and then advances `opt` to `pdu->token[256]`.

Sink. Fallthrough to case `0x0d` performs the second required extension-byte read from `pdu->token[256]`, which is the first byte beyond the 262-byte heap region allocated in step 1. ASan reports this 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at address `0x6120000008c6`.

allocation_context.note: The ASan allocation stack points to `coap_pdu_init` line 104. For the 259-byte witness, that call allocates `min(size, 256) + COAP_PDU_MAX_TCP_HEADER_SIZE = 256 + 6 = 262` bytes, matching the reported region size.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The patch replaces the vulnerable order with `size_t optsize = next_option_safe(&opt, &length, &pdu->max_opt); const uint32_t len = optsize ? coap_opt_length((const uint8_t *)opt - optsize) : 0; if (optsize == 0) return 0;`, so a one-byte trailing `0x6e` option is rejected as malformed before any `coap_opt_length()` extension-byte read occurs.

poc.trigger: PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_26371 run --version vulnerable --expect crash

format.name: 259-byte UDP CoAP packet witness
format.contract: Exact packet bytes: header `50 20 20 20`, then `0x20` repeated 254 times, then final byte `0x6e`. The trigger semantics are specific to this layout: the 255-byte post-header option region is 254 one-byte zero-length options followed by a lone `0x6e` header, so after the loop reaches that final byte with `length == 1`, `coap_opt_length()` interprets low nibble `0x0e` as an extended length and the second extension-byte read crosses the heap allocation.
